consensus_summary: Fruit symbolizes observable character, conduct, works, or results that reveal an underlying spiritual or moral condition, ordinarily applied to persons but capable of broader contextual applications.
book_summary: Fruit signifies a nation’s works or conduct, on the basis of which that nation is judged.
consensus_core_identification: Visible works or moral-spiritual outcomes that disclose the quality of their source.
book_core_identification: The visible works of a nation that disclose its quality and form the basis of judgment.
boundary_disagreement: The book restricts the symbol to collective national works and judgment, whereas the consensus treats fruit more broadly as the works, character, or results of persons and other agents, including Spirit-produced virtues and ministry outcomes.
material_contradiction: None. A nation’s works are a recognizable collective instance of the consensus category of outward moral produce.
rationale: The book retains the consensus’s central identification of fruit with observable works or outcomes but materially narrows its extension to nations and their judgment. Matthew 21:43 directly supplies that national application, while Matthew 7:17 supplies the general good-tree/good-fruit principle.
strongest_objection: Matthew 7:17 does not itself specify nations or explicitly describe judicial assessment, so the book’s formulation depends chiefly on Matthew 21:43 and on combining the two passages rather than on both independently expressing the complete definition.
